differences.title: 1. SCHEMA EVOLUTION
differences.leftDesc: Avro handles schema evolution via reader and writer schemas, allowing dynamic field addition/removal without code changes. It gracefully handles missing fields with defaults.
differences.rightDesc: Protobuf uses field tags for evolution. Adding fields is safe, but removing or reusing tags can break compatibility. Requires careful management of schema versions.

differences.title: 2. DATA ENCODING
differences.leftDesc: Avro data includes the schema, making it self-describing. This is great for data lakes and archival, but results in larger payloads compared to Protobuf.
differences.rightDesc: Protobuf encodes data efficiently with field numbers and wire types. The schema is separate, leading to smaller serialized messages, ideal for high-throughput systems.

differences.title: 3. LANGUAGE SUPPORT
differences.leftDesc: Avro has mature libraries for Java, Python, C++, and others, with excellent integration into big data ecosystems like Hadoop and Spark.
differences.rightDesc: Protobuf offers robust code generation for numerous languages including C++, Java, Python, Go, and JavaScript, making it versatile for polyglot environments.

differences.title: 4. SCHEMA DEFINITION
differences.leftDesc: Avro schemas are defined in JSON, offering human readability and ease of integration with JSON-based tools. Schemas can be embedded directly in data files.
differences.rightDesc: Protobuf uses its own .proto syntax, which is concise and powerful for defining message structures, services, and enumerations.

differences.title: 5. USE CASES
differences.leftDesc: Avro excels in big data scenarios like Hadoop, Kafka, and data warehousing due to its dynamic schema handling and self-describing data. Efficient for batch processing.
differences.rightDesc: Protobuf is widely adopted for inter-service communication (gRPC) and efficient data exchange in microservices architectures due to its performance and compactness.

differences.title: 6. NULL HANDLING
differences.leftDesc: Avro explicitly supports nulls via union types (e.g., `["null", "string"]`), making nullability clear and manageable within the schema definition.
differences.rightDesc: Protobuf fields are optional by default. For primitive types, absence implies a default value (0, false, empty string). For message fields, absence means null.

differences.title: 7. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: Avro offers solid serialization/deserialization speeds suitable for many applications, especially within its big data context where throughput is key.
differences.rightDesc: Protobuf is optimized for speed and minimal overhead, often outperforming Avro in raw serialization/deserialization benchmarks due to its compact binary format.
